newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes extend gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes extend gains in late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes saw continued strength late Monday as spot prices topped morning highs and a late-Friday crude sale tightened discounts for Alaska crude.
A spot cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold late Friday at $1.70 a barrel under bellwether West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for January delivery, traders said.
ANS prices jumped $1.30 from Friday to $23.90/24.10 a barrel.
Buyers said some potential customers remained for January cargoes of Alaska North Slope crude. Later this week, Canadian light crudes will be offered ahead of a deadline for shipping apportionments.
Line 63 was priced exclusively off a posting basis, traders said, with premiums talked $0.95 to $1.05 in the thinly traded market.
Discounts for Kern River heavy crude remained 10 cents under postings to even with postings, traders said.
Several local produces offered heavy barrels in the market, and there were late reports Chevron raised its posted prices.
Kern outright prices stayed $17.40/17.50 a barrel.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., continued to range $18.85/18.95.
